intro: Armenian media today focus on a physical brawl in parliament and Prime Minister Pashinyan's controversial characterization of the 1990 Declaration of Independence as "anti-state." Other prominent topics include Armenia's upcoming biometric document rollout, economic measures regarding inflation and oil imports, wrestling successes at the World Championships, and continued assistance for displaced Karabakh residents.

topics.title: Brawl erupts in Armenian parliament
topics.text: Physical altercations broke out between lawmakers during a parliamentary session. Prime Minister Pashinyan subsequently praised the actions of his Civil Contract faction members, stating that such confrontations will continue. The ruling majority faction called a closed session following the incident.

topics.title: Pashinyan labels Declaration of Independence 'anti-state'
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan declared that the text of Armenia's 1990 Declaration of Independence is "anti-state." He linked this assessment to the goal of making peace with Azerbaijan irreversible and suggested the matter is unlikely to lead to snap parliamentary elections. The statement drew criticism from opposition circles.

topics.title: Armenia to launch biometric passports and ID cards on November 1
topics.text: The government has approved the procedure for issuing new biometric passports and identity cards, with the system set to launch on November 1. The move aims to modernize identification documents and enhance security features for citizens.

topics.title: Central Bank vows to contain inflation amid potential Russian gas price hike
topics.text: Armenia's Central Bank pledged to keep inflation in check should Russia raise gas prices. Separately, the government adopted a new decision on oil product imports, and the finance minister discussed development cooperation with a visiting Saudi Arabian delegation.

topics.title: Armenian wrestlers advance at World Championships
topics.text: Vazgen Tevanyan reached the final of the World Wrestling Championships despite competing with a broken finger, defeating a two-time world champion en route. Tevanyan will compete for the gold medal, while other Armenian wrestlers also recorded victories in earlier rounds.

topics.title: Social assistance extended for displaced Karabakh residents through 2027
topics.text: Armenia will extend social assistance programs for forcibly displaced Nagorno-Karabakh residents through 2027. However, reports indicate the amount of financial assistance to vulnerable families is set to be sharply reduced. The government also discussed expanding universal health insurance coverage.

topics.title: Constitutional reform plans face domestic and external challenges
topics.text: Armenia's parliament ratified the TRIPP agreement but lacks the two-thirds majority required for constitutional changes. The justice minister stated the internal agenda is to write a new constitution rather than amend the current one. CivilNet reports that reform plans remain at odds with Baku's demands.
